I'm an applied AI scientist (Ph.D., EE) building perception models that are **natively
aware of the sensing physics of their data** — at the intersection of **synthetic
aperture radar (SAR)**, **complex-valued neural networks**, and **geospatial foundation
models** — rather than treating signals as generic pixels.

My through-line is hybrid, phenomenology-aware machine learning: my Ph.D. fused the
mechanics of SAR image formation and RF signal processing with deep learning to beat
conventional computer vision, and I've carried that approach from radar imaging into
operational Earth observation. I'm currently **Lead AI Scientist at Privateer Space**;
previously KBR, Microsoft, Apple, IMEC, and Texas Instruments.

What I care about most is pointing these methods at **geospatial humanitarian and
agricultural problems** — sustainable, local-scale solutions to global challenges, like
cloud-blind deforestation monitoring where optical alerts go quiet for half the year.

Recent threads:

- **Phase-aware SAR learning.** Complex-valued, coherence-preserving models for
  change detection — SAR carries structure in phase that intensity-only pipelines discard.
- **Geospatial foundation models on new sensors.** Quantifying where C-band-pretrained
  foundation models break on L-band data (NISAR) and how to close the gap.
- **Remote sensing for good.** Cloud-blind deforestation monitoring over the Colombian
  Amazon, where optical alerts go quiet for half the year.

See [**Projects**](projects.qmd) for what I'm building, the [**Blog**](blog.qmd) for
write-ups, and my [**CV**](cv.qmd) for the longer version.
